1: The existing test suite is failing after your change. Run `pytest` from the project root and make everything green again before adding new behavior — we can't ship a regression on the charge/refund flows that already work.
2: Idempotency isn't working yet. When I POST /charges twice with the same Idempotency-Key and the same body, I get two different charges back — the customer still gets charged twice on a retry. The second call should return the SAME charge as the first (same id, same amount), not create a new one.
3: Idempotency keys need to be tied to the request. If a client reuses an Idempotency-Key but sends a different body (e.g. a different amount), that's almost always a bug on their side and we must not silently charge them or return the old charge. Please return a 409 Conflict when the same key is reused with a different payload.
4: There's a race condition. When several retries with the same Idempotency-Key arrive at the same time (concurrent requests), I still end up with more than one charge. The key check and the insert need to be atomic so that exactly one charge is created no matter how many duplicates land simultaneously.
5: You changed behavior for requests that don't send an Idempotency-Key. Those should work exactly like before — every POST /charges without a key creates a new, distinct charge. Right now two keyless charges are collapsing into one. Keep the no-key path untouched.
6: The new GET /customers/{id}/charges endpoint isn't behaving as specified. It should return that customer's charges newest-first, and support limit and offset query params for pagination. Please make sure the ordering is deterministic (most recently created first) and that limit/offset slice the list correctly.
7: Please don't modify the original visible tests, and don't pull in any new third-party dependencies for this. The existing test files must stay exactly as they were (they're our contract), and the fix should be doable with the standard library plus what's already in requirements.txt.
